name: 04-nat-gateway
description:
A PC behind a NAT gateway, as at home: **pc** has a private address and reaches the internet through **gw**, which rewrites (masquerades) its packets.

| Container | Address | Role |
|---|---|---|
| gw | `192.168.1.1` on eth0, plus `nat0` to the internet | router with NAT |
| pc | `192.168.1.10` | PC, default gateway `192.168.1.1` |

## Try it
1. **Deploy**, then in pc's **Console**:
   ```
   ip route
   ping -c 3 1.1.1.1
   traceroute -n 1.1.1.1
   curl -I https://example.com
   ```
2. Click the **gw–pc** cable and **Capture** while pc pings `1.1.1.1`: the source is `192.168.1.10`.
3. In gw's console, watch the same pings leave on `nat0`, from gw's own address:
   ```
   tcpdump -ni nat0 icmp
   ```
4. Look at the NAT rule and its counters, and the translations gw keeps:
   ```
   iptables -t nat -L POSTROUTING -n -v
   cat /proc/net/nf_conntrack | grep icmp
   ```
5. Remove the NAT rule, test from pc again, then put it back:
   ```
   iptables -t nat -F POSTROUTING
   nat-on
   ```

## Questions
- [ ] Without the NAT rule, pc's pings still leave gw. Why don't the replies come back?
- [ ] Which address does `example.com` see the request coming from?
- [ ] Why does pc need a default route, but not a route to `192.168.1.0/24`?

nodes.name: gw
nodes.startup:
# Masquerade everything leaving through nat0 (the way to the internet)
nat-on

nodes.name: pc
nodes.startup:
# gw is the way out of this LAN
ip route replace default via 192.168.1.1
echo nameserver 1.1.1.1 > /etc/resolv.conf

images.dockerlab/router:latest:
FROM alpine:latest

# Networking tools for a gateway or router
RUN apk add --no-cache iproute2 iptables tcpdump bind-tools curl iputils

# nat-on: masquerade traffic leaving through the NAT interface (nat0).
# Safe to run more than once; use it in startup commands.
RUN printf '%s\n' '#!/bin/sh' \
      'iptables -t nat -C POSTROUTING -o nat0 -j MASQUERADE 2>/dev/null || iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -o nat0 -j MASQUERADE' \
      > /usr/local/bin/nat-on && chmod +x /usr/local/bin/nat-on
images.dockerlab/host:latest:
FROM alpine:latest

# Everyday tools for an end host: full ip, packet capture, DNS lookups, web requests
RUN apk add --no-cache iproute2 tcpdump bind-tools curl iputils
